sample_or_scope: 12 cities; Round II 2006-07
plain_finding: Provides the earliest nationally coordinated city mapping used in the Pakistan time series and documents a predominantly home and street market
relevance_to_paper1: Direct input to the deterioration-to-2011 comparison

sample_or_scope: 34,480 FSWs in 7 cities
sex_work_marker: population size; venue type; client volume
plain_finding: Large city differences were present; about 40% were street based and 57.5% home based while client volume was highly uneven
relevance_to_paper1: Supports use of multiple markers and city heterogeneity rather than one national average

sample_or_scope: national sex-work and HIV-prevention context
economic_or_structural_driver: poverty stigma law and programme environment
plain_finding: Describes the social and programme setting in which Pakistani sex work is organised and reached
relevance_to_paper1: Provides national context for why visibility and mapping coverage can change

sample_or_scope: 730 women selling sex in Lahore
plain_finding: Ninety-one percent cited poverty or financial reasons for entry and 99% economic survival for continuation; median duration was 7 years
relevance_to_paper1: Direct Pakistani support for economic entry and persistence mechanisms but not population change

sample_or_scope: 20 cities; 89,178 mapped FSWs
plain_finding: Provides the strongest common-round city mapping and behavioural data in the available Pakistani series
relevance_to_paper1: Primary outcome source for Paper 1

sample_or_scope: 89,178 FSWs in 15 reported city units from 2011 mapping
plain_finding: Average density was 7.2 per 1,000 adult men; 55% of the mapped population was in Karachi and Lahore and organisation varied sharply by city
relevance_to_paper1: Direct source for Paper 1 outcomes and proof that density alone misses scale and structure

sample_or_scope: 6,987 FSW observations across 9 common cities in 2006 and 2011
economic_or_structural_driver: structural vulnerability and changing work organisation
plain_finding: Mapped estimates increased from 49,037 to 73,675; cellphone solicitation and intermediary forms increased and reported client volume rose while participant profiles became more vulnerable
relevance_to_paper1: Closest published within-Pakistan corroboration of expansion plus structural change; authors note improved mapping could contribute

sample_or_scope: Round IV mapping and IBBS in 20 cities
plain_finding: Reports 89,178 mapped FSWs and describes the national second-generation surveillance system and its changing city coverage
relevance_to_paper1: Validates the provenance and limitations of the 2011 stock measure

sample_or_scope: 2011 mapped key populations and programme cost data
plain_finding: Shows how 2011 population-size estimates were used to prioritise the largest city populations and estimate programme coverage costs
relevance_to_paper1: Shows that absolute counts have direct policy meaning distinct from density

sample_or_scope: 2011 density and surveillance data from 6 cities; models in 4
economic_or_structural_driver: city heterogeneity and sexual-drug network bridging
plain_finding: FSW density and bridging varied substantially by city and required locally tailored interpretation
relevance_to_paper1: Reinforces the city-level and multi-marker approach; does not test economics

sample_or_scope: Lahore Faisalabad Multan and Sargodha
plain_finding: Provides comparable post-2011 city counts and typology shares for four Punjab cities
relevance_to_paper1: Direct input to the early-recovery comparison

sample_or_scope: national key-population mapping
plain_finding: Documents the later mapping exercise but the acquired excerpt lacks the full city tables needed for a clean longitudinal analysis
relevance_to_paper1: Supports later-round provenance while defining missingness

sample_or_scope: 18 printed city averages in Round V
plain_finding: Provides later city counts; the printed city values and grand total are internally inconsistent and no comparable density or typology table is available
relevance_to_paper1: Direct input to the long-recovery plateau test with explicit caution

sample_or_scope: 4 surveillance rounds across up to 20 cities
sex_work_marker: HIV incidence and prevalence by key population
plain_finding: Modelled epidemic trajectories differed sharply by city and key population
relevance_to_paper1: Supports avoiding pooled national assumptions; outcome is HIV rather than FSW population

sample_or_scope: 10 purposively sampled respondents in Sahiwal
plain_finding: Reports socioeconomic causes and social adjustment problems among a very small local sample
relevance_to_paper1: Locally relevant but too small and weakly sampled to support prevalence or trend claims

sample_or_scope: reported Pakistani sample
economic_or_structural_driver: poverty illiteracy low pay stigma and gender inequality
plain_finding: Identifies poverty low pay illiteracy and social exclusion as reported entry conditions
relevance_to_paper1: Adds Pakistani livelihood context but methods and normative framing limit inferential weight

sample_or_scope: eastern Zimbabwe communities across economic collapse
economic_or_structural_driver: economic collapse social norms and currency change
plain_finding: Economic collapse reduced some formal commercial activity but increased poverty-driven and commodity-based sex and dispersed negotiation into less visible community settings
relevance_to_paper1: Closest analogue to Pakistan's expansion plus homeward or less-visible reorganisation

sample_or_scope: three decades of epidemiological behavioural and economic data
economic_or_structural_driver: economic decline layoffs migrant labour and recovery
sex_work_marker: client demand; client volume; STI; sex-work activity
plain_finding: Male demand and client volumes fell during collapse as migrant workers lost jobs and activity rose again after recovery
relevance_to_paper1: Shows the countervailing demand side: worsening conditions may increase supply while reducing paid demand

sample_or_scope: 20 sites using 2015-17 RDS mapping and programme data
plain_finding: National FSW size was estimated at 40,491 with wide plausibility bounds and large differences by method and site
relevance_to_paper1: Shows why mapped counts are estimates with method-sensitive uncertainty and why site composition matters

sample_or_scope: 10 women who experienced adolescent sex work and migration
economic_or_structural_driver: family instability school fees political upheaval and livelihood need
plain_finding: Economic and family disruptions catalysed entry and sex work then generated further income-seeking migration
relevance_to_paper1: Supports shock-driven entry and mobility but the sample is small and selected

sample_or_scope: 2,591 FSWs in 2013 and 2,839 in 2016 across 14 sites
economic_or_structural_driver: search for clients with more money
plain_finding: Work travel rose from 27% to 59%; finding wealthier clients was the most common reason for travel
relevance_to_paper1: Shows that economic conditions can change geography and visibility rather than only local headcounts

sample_or_scope: 192 self-reported diaries in western Kenya
plain_finding: Women increased risky higher-paid transactional sex after unexpected household health shocks
relevance_to_paper1: Strong direct evidence that income need changes supply at short time scales

sample_or_scope: more than 200,000 people in 21 DHS surveys
plain_finding: Recent drought shocks increased HIV risk in endemic rural areas; the authors identify transactional sex as a mechanism consistent with the pattern
relevance_to_paper1: Strong causal-style evidence for income-shock pathways but outcome is HIV not FSW stock

sample_or_scope: 2015-16 DHS linked to a six-month drought
plain_finding: Among women working in agriculture a six-month drought doubled transactional sex and increased reported STI by 48%
relevance_to_paper1: Direct evidence that worsening livelihoods can increase transactional-sex supply

sample_or_scope: counties exposed to the 1861-65 cotton famine
economic_or_structural_driver: localized recession in female-employing textile industry
plain_finding: The recession increased establishments by about 20%; roughly three-quarters of the increase occurred in informal venues despite evidence of weaker leisure demand
relevance_to_paper1: Strongest direct causal evidence for downturn-driven supply and informal reorganisation; historical and legal context differs

sample_or_scope: independent indoor sex workers followed after the 2007-08 crisis
economic_or_structural_driver: austerity economic decline and weak mainstream labour market
plain_finding: Financial hardship made sex work a coping option while rising competition and declining demand worsened earnings and wellbeing
relevance_to_paper1: Clearly articulates simultaneous supply expansion and demand contraction

sample_or_scope: 42 current and former FSWs drawn from a cohort of 500
plain_finding: All but one had quit at least once; most experienced quit-re-entry cycles and economic circumstances had the strongest influence on leaving
relevance_to_paper1: Direct support for a stock that persists despite individual exits and for economically driven re-entry

sample_or_scope: 130 of an original 354 women with outcomes over 15 years
plain_finding: Fifty-nine percent were still in the sex industry after a mean 13.6 years of selling sex despite considerable occupational mobility
relevance_to_paper1: Strong evidence that sex-work population stock can remain because careers are often long

sample_or_scope: 70 FSWs in Kigali
economic_or_structural_driver: poverty disruptive events and financial crisis
plain_finding: Poverty shaped entry; financial reasons prevented leaving and some women returned after a new financial crisis
relevance_to_paper1: Direct support for economic entry barriers and re-entry

sample_or_scope: 21 Black women selling sex on the street
plain_finding: Economic necessity and lack of alternative employment constrained exit; narratives included return after losing a non-sex-work job
relevance_to_paper1: Supports plateau and return-to-work mechanisms but is a small local sample

sample_or_scope: 205 street-based FSWs followed quarterly for 12 months
economic_or_structural_driver: homelessness IPV drug treatment and income dependence
plain_finding: Forty percent stopped at least once; homelessness and IPV reduced the chance of interruption and 10% stopped then restarted
relevance_to_paper1: Quantitative evidence that leaving is non-linear and structural vulnerability sustains the stock

sample_or_scope: Indian literature on women's entry into sex work
economic_or_structural_driver: financial insecurity family discord violence coercion and independence
plain_finding: Financial insecurity was one of several recurrent entry pathways and family/community relationships shaped early careers
relevance_to_paper1: Comparable South Asian evidence that economics acts with social and coercive factors rather than alone

sample_or_scope: 5,498 mobile FSWs in 22 districts across 4 states
economic_or_structural_driver: poor economic conditions negative life events coercion and tradition
plain_finding: Poor economic conditions were a common entry reason and were associated with greater current risk than entry by choice or tradition
relevance_to_paper1: Large comparable South Asian sample supporting heterogeneous but often economic entry

sample_or_scope: sex-worker communities and programmes in Nairobi
economic_or_structural_driver: pandemic restrictions and loss of income
sex_work_marker: demand; income; food housing and health security
plain_finding: Curfews and lost income sharply harmed sex workers and changed work in ways that increased vulnerability
relevance_to_paper1: Shows that a negative shock can contract demand and harm existing workers even if supply pressure rises

sample_or_scope: 204 unique studies; 87 examined structural determinants
economic_or_structural_driver: law violence stigma work environment and community organisation
sex_work_marker: HIV risk and access among FSWs
plain_finding: Structural conditions interact with interpersonal and individual factors; single-factor explanations are inadequate
relevance_to_paper1: Provides the framework for interpreting economic conditions as one layer in a complex system

sample_or_scope: 19 papers from 16 studies
plain_finding: Transactional sex was associated with HIV among women; evidence on causal pathways was limited by few longitudinal studies
relevance_to_paper1: Clarifies that transactional-sex findings support mechanism but are not identical to FSW population estimates

sample_or_scope: 48 studies published 2000-2022
economic_or_structural_driver: orphanhood violence substance use and social vulnerability
plain_finding: Pooled reported prevalence was 12.55% with strong heterogeneity; violence orphanhood and other vulnerabilities were associated factors
relevance_to_paper1: Shows the wider vulnerability context and limits of reducing transactional sex to income alone

sample_or_scope: copper-mining cities compared through the early-2000s boom
plain_finding: The copper boom substantially reduced transactional sex and multiple partnerships in mining cities
relevance_to_paper1: Direct evidence for the opposite-side question: improved economic conditions can reduce transactional sex

sample_or_scope: sex workers randomized to improved outside-work incentives or unconditional cash
plain_finding: Improving outside-work incentives raised outside earnings 20% and reduced sex work 13%; an unconditional cash transfer did not reduce sex work
relevance_to_paper1: Direct evidence that better alternative employment can reduce sex-work supply; working paper status requires later publication check

sample_or_scope: 30 FSWs interviewed three times over 12 months in Blantyre
economic_or_structural_driver: income instability business failure partner loss violence and stigma
plain_finding: Twenty of 30 had temporarily left at least once and most returned when circumstances worsened; financial stability supported slowing or breaks
relevance_to_paper1: Recent longitudinal support for a dynamic stock with temporary exit and economically driven re-entry
